resolutions.researcher_notes: NS Energy (project profile, live, updated Nov 2024) describes commissioning in 2004, an ~8-month shutdown during the 2011 conflict, and ongoing operation since — status is inferable/current. OGJ (Oct 2011, seed citation, verified live) independently reports Eni/NOC resuming Greenstream gas throughput after the 2011 conflict, confirming the line returned to and remains in operating status. Two independent origins (trade press, different dates) agree; no source suggests the line is shelved/cancelled/mothballed today.
Both NS Energy and Saipem (the pipeline's original EPC contractor, primary source) describe Greenstream/LGTS explicitly as a natural gas transmission pipeline. Uncontested, trivial to corroborate.

Saipem's own official project page (primary source — Saipem was the main pipelay contractor) states 'Construction Years: 2002-2004', directly supporting ConstructionYear=2002 as the start year. Energy Circle (trade news, independent outlet) separately reports 'Originally installed by Saipem in 2002'. FLAG: other tertiary sources (Wikipedia, NS Energy) instead say construction 'started in 2003' — we prefer the primary contractor source (Saipem) plus independent corroboration (Energy Circle) over the tertiary 2003 claim, but note the 2002/2003 conflict for the record.

StartYear1=2004 is well corroborated: Wikipedia infobox 'Commissioned 2004' (supplies started 1 Oct 2004, inaugurated 7 Oct 2004) and NS Energy 'it started operations in 2004' agree, and match the seed Reuters/OGJ Oct-2011 restart coverage's framing of Greenstream as commissioned pre-2011. StartYear2=2006 (likely the year the line reached its expanded ~11 bcm/y capacity per Wikipedia's 'later the capacity was increased to 11 bcm', undated) could NOT be independently confirmed to the year 2006 specifically in any live source found — left supported only by the 2004 primary start date; flagging 2006 as unconfirmed rather than fabricating a cite for it.

Could not find any source supporting Capacity=20.00 MMcf/d. Every source checked (Wikipedia, NS Energy, RT Arabic, greenstreambv.com official site) states Greenstream's nameplate capacity as 8 bcm/y initially, expanded to 11 bcm/y — i.e. roughly 770-1,060 MMcf/d, not 20 MMcf/d (a ~50x discrepancy). 20 MMcf/d does not match any sub-component either (the domestic-supply spur is documented at 'up to 15 MSCM' per greenstreambv.com, a different and much larger figure). Likely a unit-label or data-entry error already present in the mainsheet (e.g. 8 bcm/y ≈ 21.9 million m3/day ≈ 20 MMcm/d, which is close to '20' but in MMcm/d, not MMcf/d as labeled). Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that supports a different number under the same label — flagging the contradiction for review rather than silently fabricating support.

Wood Mackenzie's asset summary states 'The total length of the pipeline is 520 kilometres, all subsea' — an exact match to the sheet's 520.00 km. Energy Circle independently states 'The pipeline extends 520 kilometres from Mellitah...to Gela'. Other sources cluster close (Saipem/NS Energy/greenstreambv.com: 516-518 km offshore-only measure; Wikipedia infobox: 520 km; Wikipedia body text: 540 km; PPSA/Weatherford PDF: 518 km) — 520 km is the most frequently and most precisely corroborated figure, consistent with the GEM value.

RT Arabic (verified live, seed citation) is a strong single-source match for the exact compound value '36, 32, 10 in': it describes a 10-inch line carrying gas from the Sabratha offshore platform to Mellitah, a 32-inch line exporting to Italy, and a 36-inch line for domestic Libyan supply — all three diameters named. PPSA/Weatherford PDF (pdftotext-recovered, seed citation) independently corroborates only the 32-inch export line ('32 inch 322 mile (518km) pipeline'), not the 36in/10in laterals, so this is not full 2-source independent corroboration of the whole compound value — set to medium/single-strong-source per confidence_tiers.md rather than high.

The mainsheet's FuelSource field itself holds this RT Arabic URL as its literal 'value' (an ingestion quirk — a citation link stored in a data cell rather than a fuel-source name). Verified the URL is live (200) and on-topic: it's a substantive Arabic-language article naming the actual fuel sources feeding Greenstream — gas processed at the Sabratha offshore platform (~110 km off Tripoli) and the onshore Wafa ('Wafi') field — so the stored value is itself a legitimate, verifiable reference, not a fabrication. Re-affirmed rather than replaced since it already satisfies standing rule 3 (real, verified, on-topic, non-GEM) at medium/single-source confidence; note the article's claim of a 2007 inauguration conflicts with the widely corroborated Oct 2004 date (see Construction/Start notes) so its other historical claims should be read with some caution, though the fuel-source/diameter details it gives line up well with independent sources.

Both NS Energy and Saipem (independent origins) confirm the route runs from the Mellitah complex, Libya to Gela, Sicily, Italy — matching StartLocation/EndLocation exactly. Universally consistent across every source checked in this research (Wikipedia, greenstreambv.com, RT Arabic, PPSA).

Wikipedia body text states 'The construction cost US$6.6 billion' (url_verifier's automated substring screen missed this — 'US$6.6 billion' has no space before the dollar figure, a screen false-negative; confirmed manually by reading the full fetched page). RT Arabic (independent origin) separately states 'the project cost $6.6 billion USD'. Two independent sources agreeing on the identical figure — note Wikipedia's own citation trail for this figure traces to a dead 2004 'Alexander's Gas & Oil Connections' article we could not independently re-verify, so treat Wikipedia here as corroboration rather than sole authority; RT Arabic is the stronger of the two. NS Energy separately gives $700 million for just the Mellitah Gas Compression Station component, which is consistent with (a subset of) the $6.6B total project cost, not a contradiction.

GreenStream BV's own official company page (primary source, the owning JV itself) states its two equal shareholders are 'Eni North Africa BV (owned by Eni S.p.a.)' at 50% and 'NOC (National Oil Corporation)' at 50% — directly confirming Owner1=Eni SpA / Owner2=Libyan National Oil Corp. NS Energy (independent trade source) corroborates: 'a joint venture of Eni North Africa (50%) and National Oil Corporation of Libya (NOC) (50%)'. Primary + independent secondary in full agreement.
